numbering_direction.summary: On EVERY seating level, section numbers start on the THIRD BASE / left-field-line side and INCREASE toward home plate, then toward FIRST BASE and RIGHT FIELD. The 100 (Mezzanine) and 200 (Pavilion) levels then continue the wrap all the way around through center field and end in left field (so the highest numbers on those two levels, ~136-142 and ~239-244, are back in left field, adjacent to where 101/201 start). The 300 (Upper) level does not wrap - it runs foul pole to foul pole, 301 at third base to 326 at the right field corner. The lower level (1-33) runs 1 at the third base corner to 26 at the first base corner, then sections 27-33 are the left-field lower/All-You-Can-Eat group (a numbering discontinuity).
numbering_direction.one_line: Numbers increase from third base toward first base / right field (low = third base side, high = first base side).

accessibility.summary: Globe Life Field provides wheelchair-accessible and companion seating on every seating level, generally located at the TOP of sections on each concourse (rateyourseats: 'Accessible seating at Globe Life Field is found at the top of many sections on the main concourse'). Accessible seats are raised so standing fans in front do not block sightlines. Accessible tickets are bought by phone at 972-RANGERS (972-726-4377), at rangers.com/tickets, or online by selecting 'Yes, show accessible seating.' Complimentary wheelchair escort service runs between the gates and ticketed seats. Season-ticket holders can exchange regular seats for accessible seats at no cost via sth_exchange@texasrangers.com. Service animals are permitted per ADA. Sensory room and assistive listening devices are available.

discovery.row_seat_conventions: ROWS ARE NUMBERS at Globe Life Field, not letters. Every section page checked (1, 5, 12, 19, 26, 33, 101, 105, 114, 121, 125, 130, 134, 136, 140, 201, 222, 227, 232, 244, 301, 305, 313, 320, 322, 326) shows numeric rows. Typical ranges: lower level rows 1-16; mezzanine infield rows 1-20; right field mezzanine up to rows 1-28/30; left field mezzanine rows 1-9 to 1-11; Pavilion rows 1-13; Upper level rows 1-14. Some sections do not start at Row 1 (Section 19 is rows 3-16; Section 26 is rows 9-16). Row 1 is closest to the field in most sections, but many sections are entered from the BACK - rateyourseats notes 'An entrance to this section is located at Row 20' for mezzanine infield sections and Row 28 for right field mezzanine - while Upper Level sections are entered at Row 1 (you walk up from the 200 concourse). SEAT NUMBERING: uniform park-wide - facing the field, seat 1 is on the left, seat numbers increase to the right. Consequence: on the FIRST BASE side seat 1 is the seat closest to home plate; on the THIRD BASE side the HIGH seat numbers are closest to home plate.
discovery.seat1_side_verbatim: "When looking towards the stage/field, lower number seats are on the left" - rateyourseats.com, appears verbatim on every Globe Life Field section page checked (e.g. sections 1, 5, 12, 101, 105, 114, 121, 130, 140, 322). Corroborated by bestballparkseats.com: "down the third base line, high seat numbers are closer to home plate" and "down the first base line, seat #1 is closest to home plate."
discovery.known_obstructions: 1) NETTING: 'The netting at Globe Life Field extends all the way into the outfield' - the protective net runs well past the dugouts, so lower-level corner boxes (sections 1-4 and 22-26) and most infield lower sections view the game through netting. 2) RAILINGS/GLASS: front rows of many elevated sections are cut by a rail or glass panel - a section 324 reviewer notes 'Rows 1 and 2 are partially obstructed by railing/glass'; a section 140 row 1 reviewer notes 'Rail is distracting.' 3) OVERHANGS: rear rows of the lower level and left field sections (e.g. section 30) sit 'under an overhang', which cuts off high fly balls and the videoboards. 4) RIGHT FIELD MEZZANINE (128-133) are the largest sections, ~28-30 rows deep with entrances at the back, so back rows are far from the field. 5) CENTER FIELD batter's eye (120 ft x 40 ft) blocks the field for anything directly behind it; Teremana Terrace (134-135) sits above it. 6) SCOREBOARD SIGHTLINES: many left field and third base sections cannot see the left field board; some upper first base sections have obstructed views of the main right field videoboard. 7) CONCERTS: upper sections such as 325-326 are behind or to the side of the stage for most concerts, which restricts the view. 8) ROOF: the retractable roof is USUALLY CLOSED for heat - 'The Rangers typically play with the roof closed, and Globe Life Field stays between 72 and 74 degrees all season long'; it takes 12-15 minutes to open or close. When open, the roof docks behind the third base grandstand. The roof and its clear panels are 193'10" above home plate; balls hitting the roof or its structure are governed by ground rules.
discovery.roof_note: Retractable roof, 5.5 acres, with clear panels. Normally CLOSED because of Texas heat; interior held at 72-74 degrees. Sun/shade is therefore mostly a non-factor for Rangers games, unlike at the old Globe Life Park.
